thread:
pagerbot: ALERT: auth-service generating high 401s (2.5k in 5m) and anomalous S3 PUTs detected from 'logshipper' role to s3://public-logs-archive/rdw/ (detected 12:03-12:09 UTC). Auto-page: #incidents
alex: i'm oncall, thanks pagerbot. paging @maya and @sec_ops. cognizant of customer impact? :eyes:
maya: ack. pulling traces and s3 access logs now. prioritizing inference-api and indexer lambdas.
sec_ops: seeing PUTs from IP 45.77.123.9 using AWS role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/logshipper. user-agent = curl/7.79.1. suspicious.
samir: we deployed an indexer forwarder yesterday, it's configured to forward debug logs to an internal bucket. checking config.
pagerbot: suspicious object keys: rdw/2026-03-20/instance-*/auth-debug-headers.log.gz ; potential auth header snippets present in file names (auto-flagged)
maya: found lines showing auth header fragments in one object. sample (redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN_SNIPPET>
User-Agent: RedwoodIndexer/1.2
```
jen: legal/PII note: preserve everything. @liaison-legal please advise on disclosure thresholds. do NOT delete objects until we snapshot for forensics.
liaison-legal: acknowledged. preserve and snapshot. if tokens or PII confirmed, we'll follow customer-notify cadence. send list of affected tenants once we have mapping.
michael: i can flip network egress rules for the forwarder. recommend blocking that role's outbound S3 and suspend the forwarder process now.
maya: rolling a temporary block on the forwarder (canary first). command i ran:
```
kubectl -n infra patch deployment log-forwarder -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"forwarder","env":[{"name":"S3_EGRESS","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'
```
maya: can confirm the forwarder stopped initiating PUTs. still seeing 3 anomalous requests (stale) finishing upload.
sec_ops: starting key/service-account rotation for indexer and logshipper. plan:
- revoke current access key for role-bound user
- create new keys and rotate in deploy pipeline
- rotate any KMS data-key if used
samir: putting a quick patch to replace the indexer credential with a short-lived role (sts assume-role) and will validate no regressions.
jen: i'll coordinate KMS rotation with infra. who can run the IAM revoke now? i'd like to ensure we rotate both programmatic keys and longer-lived tokens.
alex: @maya please revoke tokens you can, @samir do the deploy change, @sec_ops do key rotation. support, prepare customer triage list.
support: started identifying customers with logs ingested during window 12:03-12:09 UTC. flagging enterprise tenants first. template for outreach ready.
sec_ops: executing revoke commands now (audit log will contain steps). sample actions:
```
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id ABC123 --status Inactive --user-name logshipper
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id alias/rdw-indexer-key --pending-window-in-days 7
```
sec_ops: note we scheduled KMS deletion with the usual pending window; will instead rotate/data-key wrap and re-encrypt any persisted tokens.
maya: ran quick verification: no new PUTs in the last 2m after egress block. S3 access logs show 0 successful PUTs since 12:11 UTC.
jen: we captured snapshot copies of the suspect objects to a forensics bucket (restricted access). copied with read-only ACL and logged the copy operation.
liaison-legal: please provide list of object keys and affected tenant ids asap. legal will start impact assessment and escalation decision tree.
support: preliminary list attached (short): tenant-a (high), tenant-b (medium). marking high-touch accounts for outbound comms if exposure confirmed.
samir: deploy change pushed to replace secrets with sts assume-role; rollout 3/3 healthy. will monitor for errors.
maya: confirmed indexer telemetry back to normal; latency stable. 401s dropped back to baseline.
alex: sound like mitigation in place. next immediate actions: 1) complete key rotation 2) finish forensics snapshot 3) run prompt-based eval to detect PII in objects 4) prepare customer comms draft.
sec_ops: will run automated PII scan over the snapshots and deliver a short report within 2 hours.
jen: internal postmortem to be scheduled. we should include: root cause (logshipper role permitted to external bucket), why auth headers leaked to logs, and fix (redact header-level logs and tighten forwarder egress policy).
liaison-legal: if PII found we need to notify affected customers within SLA window. keep legal in loop on any live findings.
alex: thanks team. marks: incident -> mitigated. keeping channel open for artifacts and forensics notes. will convert to postmortem channel after initial report.
pagerbot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, alerted=9, responders=8, mitigation=egress-block+key-rotation+snapshot
support: prepping initial customer outreach template for tenant-a; will hold until legal signoff.
jen: rotation and scans in flight. will update in thread. good work everyone :thumbsup:
